content.text:
Only Sr2ScGaO5 (mp-1105158) is present.

The strongest observed peaks are a group of three at about 29.90°, 31.05° and 31.85° two-theta, with heights of roughly 30, 39 and 100. The simulated Sr2ScGaO5 pattern has the same three peaks, with the same spacing (23 and 16 grid steps) and similar heights. It also accounts for the weaker peaks near 22.95° and 24.45°, the small peak near 32.95°, and a strong peak of about 33 at higher angle.

I simulated seven of the nine candidates. The other six (YbMn4(CuO4)3, CaCr4(CuO4)3, TiNi4GeO8, Er2Cu(GeO3)4, ZnFe(SiO3)2 and NaMnO2) do not have this group of three peaks. Their strongest peaks fall where the observed pattern has none. The spinel TiNi4GeO8, for example, puts its strongest peak at about 35.6°, and the observed pattern has nothing there.

I did not simulate Li2AlFeO4 (mp-755803) or Sr3LaTaAl3O12 (mp-1232342). I also only compared the higher-angle part of the pattern by eye, so I can't completely rule out a weak second phase.

{"present": ["mp-1105158"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "The observed strong peaks at about 29.9, 31.05 and 31.85 degrees, and the weaker ones near 23 and 24.5 degrees, match the simulated Sr2ScGaO5 pattern in position and height, and no peaks clearly call for a second phase."}
